data.one_liner: Advanced HTTP network inspector and logger with a native UI for Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Alice intercepts REST API requests and responses to provide a built-in on-device UI for inspecting headers, bodies, response times, and timelines. It supports major HTTP clients like Dio, http, Chopper, and GraphQL.
use_when: You need to inspect and debug HTTP traffic directly on-device without setting up an external proxy.
You want a searchable visual history of all REST API requests, responses, and timeline metrics during development.
avoid_when: You are running a production release where network logging and interception could leak sensitive information or degrade performance.
You do not use REST/GraphQL HTTP clients compatible with Alice's interceptor adapters.
strengths: Broad compatibility with popular Dart HTTP clients including Dio, http, Chopper, Retrofit, and GraphQL.
Rich on-device UI features like interactive JSON/XML viewers, request replay, statistics dashboard, and a floating overlay bubble.
Capture-time security redaction for sensitive headers and body keys.
weaknesses: Requires adding client-specific adapter packages and wiring them into each HTTP client instance.
Increases application size and dependency footprint if many adapters are integrated.
data.setup_notes: Initialize Alice configuration, pass the navigator key to your MaterialApp, and attach the client-specific adapter (e.g., alice_dio) to your network client.

alternatives.name: pretty_dio_logger
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only use Dio and prefer seeing requests and responses formatted directly in the developer console instead of an on-device UI.

alternatives.name: talker
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a more general-purpose logging and debugging tool that handles exceptions, routing, and block events alongside network traffic.
